scope: 12 new temporary events; 2 events per condition; 3 planned evaluations per event
preconditions: All ten required returned fields exist and match the intended payload except the zone condition under test.
Returned status is confirmed and aliases identify the exact new record.
The intended zone is America/Toronto for every event.
Saved America/New_York events use the same absolute start and end times as the Toronto target, so the test isolates named-zone evidence.
The final evidence reads both zone labels from the exact event editor and cancels without saving.
success_criteria: No saved proof from a missing, unverified, or incorrect zone input.
Both positive controls produce a saved proof when complete evidence is available.
Ten correct records can produce a saved proof from valid exact-record evidence.
Both wrong named-zone records remain rejected even when UTC offsets match.
No retry creates a second event, and no proof evaluation writes to Calendar.
All 12 exact IDs are deleted and a bounded marker search has no active results.
comparison: A field-only acceptance rule that omits named-zone evidence accepts all matching connector field sets. This is a local counterfactual baseline, not a second set of website operations.
limits: These selected events are not independent samples of production failure rates.
The adapter trusts extracted evidence and does not authenticate it.
Missing end labels and incorrect supplied labels are local evidence changes, not provider errors.
The same records occur in all three phases; 36 decisions are not 36 new events.
A missing zone blocks a full-field claim even when the saved record is actually correct.
The checker is restricted to the current English Toronto labels.
